Evidence: The Supreme Court and various high courts in India have implemented measures to limit court operations due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Starting March 16, 2020, courts began hearing only urgent matters, and access was restricted to a limited number of individuals, including lawyers and litigants involved in those urgent cases (Source 1, Source 2). The Bombay High Court also announced reduced hours and restricted access to court premises (Source 1). Additionally, the Delhi High Court decided to hear only urgent matters and not insist on personal appearances unless necessary (Source 1).
Justification: The retrieved evidence confirms that starting from March 16, 2020, the Kolkata High Court, along with other courts in the state, limited operations to urgent matters only, effectively closing down regular court activities to prevent the spread of COVID-19. This aligns with the claim that all courts in the state, including the Kolkata High Court, were closed from Wednesday for infection control efforts, as stated in the evidence from Sources 1 and 2.
